ground_truth_root_cause: Deploy sha=94f8a915b080 (2026-05-13T11:48:42Z) introduced a regression in cart-service/src/repository/cart-repository.js: the exception handling path for 'item not found' errors in deleteItem() acquires a database connection but fails to release it back to the pool (missing connection.release() in the catch block). Under normal traffic, repeated DELETE requests for non-existent cart items cause the connection pool to accumulate unreleased handles, exhausting all 20 connections within ~3 minutes of deployment and triggering cascading HTTP 503/500 errors across cart-service, product-catalog, and checkout-service.
ground_truth_remediation: 1. Immediately roll back cart-service to sha=449ee7cc0d6e to restore the previous exception handling behavior and release the pool exhaustion. 2. In cart-repository.js deleteItem(), add connection.release() inside the catch block (use try/finally to guarantee release on all code paths). 3. Verify fix in staging by simulating DELETE requests for non-existent items and confirming db_conns_active returns to baseline. 4. Re-deploy the patched version with a canary rollout, monitoring connection pool utilization before full rollout.
